summary: Marathon County, WI lookout, listed as Elderon (Pike Lake), marked gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association; no build date, staffing or site description found.

facts.status_note: Forest Fire Lookout Association lists the tower as gone; no removal date or site description found in sources read

OpenStreetMap calls it the Elderon Lookout Tower
elevation 1,295 feet above sea level (MSL), about 394.7 m, which matches the OSM 395 m to the nearest meter

evidence.supports: a sighted smoke led the lookout to use binoculars and a compass table in the cab to pinpoint it (general network description)
evidence.quote: If a smoke was sighted, the lookout used a compass table situated at the center of the cab, and binoculars to pinpoint its location.

evidence.supports: readings were called in to a dispatch center (general network description)
evidence.quote: Its azimuth, and distance was called in to a dispatch center.

evidence.quote: In 2015, the 72 aging towers still in use were decommissioned.

notes_for_editor: Thin record. Specific facts come from the FFLA list (name, county, coordinates, gone), OpenStreetMap (name, 395 m), TopoQuest (1,295 ft MSL), Forest Lookouts (survey location 27N-10E-20) and the Town of Elderon homepage (Pike Lake as a lake, not the tower). No build date, design, height, staffing or removal date found. The Marathon County forest-unit page returned 403 and was not read. TopoQuest's location line is a geodata aggregator, so treat its elevation as secondary to OSM. Next steps: Wisconsin Historical Society AHI, Marathon County and Wausau newspapers, and Conservation Department reports for dates and fate.
